section_1.title: Prerequisite Review: Vectors as Arrows
section_1.content: Briefly define a vector as an ordered pair (x, y) representing displacement. Introduce the 'Grid' visualization where basis vectors i-hat (1,0) and j-hat (0,1) act as the building blocks for any point in 2D space.
section_1.example: Imagine a robot on a 2D floor; any move is a combination of horizontal (i) and vertical (j) steps.

section_2.title: Linear Combinations & Span
section_2.content: Define linear combination: c1*v1 + c2*v2. Explain 'Span' as the set of all reachable points. Visualize this as the 'area of influence' created by scaling and adding vectors.
section_2.example: If you have two vectors pointing in different directions, their 'Span' is the entire 2D plane. If they point the same way, the 'Span' is just a single line.

section_3.title: Linear Dependence: Redundancy
section_3.content: Explain that a set is linearly dependent if one vector can be formed by the others (it provides no new 'reach'). Visualize this as two vectors lying on the same line or three vectors in a flat 2D plane.
section_3.example: If you have a robot that can move North (N) and East (E), adding a third vector 'Northeast' (N+E) is redundant—it's a 'dependent' movement that doesn't increase reach.

section_4.title: Bases: The Perfect Coordinate System
section_4.content: Define a 'Basis' as a set of vectors that are (1) Linearly Independent and (2) Span the entire space. It is the minimal set of vectors needed to describe every point uniquely.
section_4.example: Using standard grid vectors (1,0) and (0,1) as a basis for a map. Any location can be described by exactly one combination of these two units.

section_5.title: Summary & Application
section_5.content: Recap: Span (reach), Independence (efficiency), and Basis (the skeleton). Connect these to data science—where variables are vectors and a 'basis' represents the most efficient way to store information.
section_5.example: In a 3D video game engine, the 'basis' defines the camera's orientation. Changing the basis allows the engine to calculate perspectives from any character's viewpoint.
